title: Tarski’s exponential function problem
formal: Is there a deterministic Turing machine which, on every first-order sentence \(\varphi\) in the language \(\{0,1,+,- ,\times ,<,\exp\}\), halts and correctly decides whether \(\varphi\) is true in \((R,0,1,+,- ,\times ,<,x\mapsto e^{x})\)?
definitions: Sentences have finite syntax and no free variables. Terms are formed from variables, 0,1, the unary symbols − and exp, and binary + and ×; atomic formulas are equalities or strict inequalities of terms. Formulas use Boolean connectives and first-order quantifiers, all ranging over R. Equality has its usual logical interpretation. Inputs are finite parenthesized strings over a fixed finite alphabet, with variable indices written in binary; any fixed effectively interconvertible syntax encoding gives the same decidability question. No arbitrary real constants or oracles for real numbers are allowed. The symbol exp denotes the standard real exponential function on all of R, not a restricted function or an unspecified solution in another structure. There is no time or space bound beyond termination. A positive resolution must be unconditional, rather than assuming an unresolved transcendence conjecture.
answer_criterion: Prove the proposition in the problem statement or its logical negation, with all definitions, promises, resource bounds and quantifiers as stated. A conditional result establishes only the explicitly conditional claim. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof-assistant-verified proof of the full target.
why: Locate a fundamental decidability boundary beyond polynomial real arithmetic, where exact reasoning interacts with transcendence.

importance.reason: A longstanding central question of real model theory with direct relevance to symbolic reasoning about exponential expressions. The explicit 2026 conditional result confirms continuing specialist interest without settling the unconditional target.

progress.text: Macintyre–Wilkie obtain conditional decidability from Schanuel’s conjecture, as recalled by the 2026 primary source.
Berarducci–Gallinaro v2 retains the Schanuel assumption for the full real exponential theory.

context_blocks.text: First-order arithmetic over the real numbers can describe polynomial equalities, inequalities and quantifier alternation. Adding the exponential function permits expressions involving growth and decay that are unavailable in the polynomial language. The target is exact truth of every sentence, including cases in which a numerical approximation alone cannot distinguish equality from a very small nonzero quantity.

The syntax is finite even though the quantified domain is infinite. An algorithm receives a formula such as an existential statement about real solutions; it does not receive an arbitrary real constant as an infinitely long input. Fixing the standard exponential function and excluding such parameters prevents representation choices from changing the decision problem.

Macintyre and Wilkie proved decidability under Schanuel’s conjecture. Berarducci and Gallinaro’s 2026 paper obtains an axiomatization under the same assumption and recovers that conditional decidability result. Its unconditional result for a related restricted exponential setting does not settle the unrestricted theory on this card.

This question is not the task of efficiently evaluating \(e^{x}\) to a specified error. Exact logical decision also includes formulas with arbitrary quantifier patterns and exact equalities. Conversely, the card imposes no polynomial running-time demand. An unconditional terminating algorithm of any complexity would answer it affirmatively.

The catalogue already contains individual questions about linear recurrences and linear dynamical systems. TCS-6265 concerns safety exactly at a specific robustness threshold, not the full elementary theory of the real exponential field. The new card supplies a broader, distinct boundary for algorithmic reasoning with real analytic operations.
